items.headline: Driver who staged 73 traffic accidents for insurance payouts jailed 32 weeks
items.summary: A Singaporean driver who orchestrated about 73 staged traffic accidents, mostly to claim cash insurance payouts, was jailed 32 weeks and fined S$6,000.

items.headline: Singapore lines up free World Cup screenings as Mediacorp airs 28 matches free-to-air
items.summary: From June 12 to July 20, the FIFA World Cup will be screened free at 52 community clubs, five ActiveSG sport centres, The Kallang and Changi Airport, while Mediacorp broadcasts 28 matches free-to-air on Channel 5 and meWATCH.

items.headline: Economists cut Singapore's 2026 growth forecast to 1.7% as Gulf conflict bites
items.summary: Private economists cut their median forecast for Singapore's 2026 growth to 1.7% from 2.6% in the latest MAS survey, and nearly three in five expect the central bank to ease policy again at its next review.

items.headline: Modi becomes India's longest-serving elected PM as NDA marks 12 years in power
items.summary: Narendra Modi on June 10 became India's longest continuously serving elected prime minister, passing Nehru's 4,398-day record, as NDA chief ministers passed a resolution praising his 12 years; the Congress dismissed the milestone as self-proclaimed.

items.headline: Fitch cuts India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.4%, citing the US-Iran war
items.summary: Fitch Ratings lowered India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.4% from 6.7% in its June Global Economic Outlook, warning that higher energy prices from the US-Iran war will erode real incomes, with growth easing from 7.4% in FY26.

items.headline: Monsoon advances into the northeast as Delhi braces for a wet spell
items.summary: The southwest monsoon advanced into the remaining northeastern states, all of Sikkim and parts of sub-Himalayan West Bengal by June 9, the IMD said, while a western disturbance is forecast to bring a wet spell over northwest India, including Delhi, until June 13.

items.headline: RBI deputy governor Swaminathan reappointed for two more years
items.summary: The government reappointed Swaminathan Janakiraman as a Reserve Bank of India deputy governor for two years from June 26, extending his oversight of banking supervision and regulation.

items.headline: Update: US strikes Iran after Apache downed in Hormuz; Iran hits Gulf bases
items.summary: The US launched waves of strikes on Iranian air-defence sites near the Strait of Hormuz late on June 9 after an American Apache helicopter was downed, and Iran retaliated early on June 10 with drone and missile attacks on US forces in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan.

items.headline: Update: Israel keeps up Lebanon strikes, says its campaign is far from over
items.summary: Israel kept up air strikes in southern Lebanon near Tyre on June 10, and Defence Minister Israel Katz said its campaign against Iran and Hezbollah was far from over; officials said a US-pressed truce had halted a planned large-scale strike on Iran.

items.headline: UK leaders urge calm after Belfast stabbing sparks anti-immigration protests
items.summary: UK political leaders urged calm after the arrest of a Sudanese man over an attempted murder in a Belfast stabbing triggered anti-immigration protests in Northern Ireland.

items.headline: Largest-ever World Cup kicks off as Mexico hosts South Africa
items.summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup, the first with 48 teams and co-hosted by the US, Mexico and Canada, kicks off on June 11 with hosts Mexico facing South Africa in Mexico City, opening a month-long, 104-match tournament.

items.headline: Update: Apple shares slide after WWDC as Wall Street splits on the Gemini-Siri bet
items.summary: Apple shares fell after its WWDC keynote, closing down 3.6% at $290.55 on June 9, as Wall Street split over its Google Gemini-powered Siri; Wedbush kept a $400 target while bears put a floor near $215, with analysts flagging the lack of a firm Siri launch date.

items.headline: Microsoft ships its largest-ever Patch Tuesday, fixing about 200 flaws
items.summary: Microsoft released its largest-ever Patch Tuesday on June 10, fixing about 200 security vulnerabilities, including three publicly disclosed zero-day flaws, surpassing its previous monthly record of 167.

items.headline: Nvidia races to meet surging China demand for its H200 AI chips
items.summary: Nvidia is scrambling to meet surging Chinese demand for its H200 AI accelerators, with reported orders far outstripping current inventory and pressure building on supplier TSMC to ramp up output.

items.headline: US inflation jumps to 4.2%, a three-year high, as energy costs surge
items.summary: US consumer prices rose 0.5% in May and 4.2% from a year earlier, the highest annual rate since 2023, as energy prices jumped 3.9% on the month and gasoline ran 40.5% higher year-on-year; core inflation was milder at 2.9%, leaving the Fed expected to hold on June 17.

items.headline: Update: Wall Street tumbles as hot CPI and US-Iran strikes hit stocks
items.summary: US stocks fell sharply on June 10 after the inflation surprise and fresh US-Iran strikes: the Dow dropped 953 points, or 1.87%, to 49,918.78, the Nasdaq lost 1.98% to 25,169.50 and the S&P 500 fell 1.62% to 7,266.99.

items.headline: Oil swings as US-Iran strikes rattle the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Brent crude swung around $91 a barrel on June 10, paring earlier gains after dropping about 3% the previous session, as traders weighed escalating US-Iran strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and a 9.1-million-barrel drop in US crude inventories to a four-month low.

items.headline: Update: SpaceX IPO four times oversubscribed before its June 12 debut
items.summary: SpaceX's record IPO is roughly four times oversubscribed ahead of pricing after the June 11 close, with shares fixed at $135 to raise about $75 billion and value the company near $1.8 trillion before its Nasdaq debut on June 12 under the ticker SPCX.

items.headline: Maybank says it has funnelled $4.9 billion into the Johor-Singapore economic zone
items.summary: Malayan Banking has facilitated about RM20 billion (US$4.9 billion) of financing and investment in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone over the past two years and helped establish nine family offices in Johor, its chief executive said.

items.headline: India lose Kohli and Hardik Pandya to injury before Afghanistan ODIs
items.summary: India suffered a double injury blow before their three-match ODI series against Afghanistan, with Virat Kohli (hamstring) and Hardik Pandya (quad strain) both ruled out; Yashasvi Jaiswal replaces Kohli, and the series opens June 13 in Dharamsala.

items.headline: India thrash Afghanistan by an innings and 300 runs in one-off Test
items.summary: India thrashed Afghanistan by an innings and 300 runs inside three days in the one-off Test at New Chandigarh, with captain Shubman Gill making 126 and debutant left-arm spinner Manav Suthar taking seven wickets, including 6 for 33 in the first innings.

items.headline: Defending champion Tatjana Maria beats Sakkari at Queen's
items.summary: Defending champion Tatjana Maria opened her title defence at the grass-court Queen's Club event with a 6-3, 6-3 win over Maria Sakkari in the first round.

items.headline: Eala and Cirstea also reach the Queen's second round
items.summary: Alexandra Eala beat Zhang Shuai 6-3, 6-2 and Sorana Cirstea edged Maddison Inglis 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to reach the second round of the WTA grass-court event at Queen's Club on June 10.

fun_fact.headline: Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not
fun_fact.body: Botanically, a banana is a berry but a strawberry is not. A true berry develops from a single flower with one ovary and carries its seeds inside the flesh, while a strawberry grows from a flower with many ovaries and bears its tiny seeds on the outside, making it an aggregate accessory fruit.

puzzle.title: The Diver in the Forest
puzzle.body: After a forest fire is put out, firefighters find the body of a man in a full scuba outfit - wetsuit, mask, flippers and air tank - lying in the middle of the burnt forest, miles from the nearest lake or sea. How did a scuba diver end up dead in the middle of a burning forest?
puzzle.approach: Forget foul play - ask how a fully equipped diver could end up far from any water, and what moves large volumes of water during a fire.
puzzle.answer: He was scuba diving in a nearby lake or sea when a firefighting aircraft, skimming low to scoop up water to dump on the blaze, accidentally sucked him up along with the water and then released its load - and the diver - over the burning forest.
